name: Forex Session Clock
when_to_pick: A 24-hour UTC timeline of the four FX trading sessions (Sydney / Tokyo / London / New York) shown as colored bands on one track, with the high-liquidity OVERLAP windows highlighted (the Tokyo+Sydney and especially the London+New York overlap). A live vertical marker sweeps to the current UTC time and the open sessions are called out. The bands render server-side, so the timeline is fully readable even before JS runs. Use it to explain why intraday FX strategies cluster around the London/NY overlap, when liquidity and volatility peak, and which hours are dead.

title.description: Heading for the timeline, e.g. 'When each FX session is open (UTC)'.

sessions.description: The trading sessions to plot on the 24h track, in display order. Times are integer UTC hours (0-24); a session that wraps midnight (e.g. Sydney 21:00-06:00) is fine — set start greater than end.

city.description: Optional city/zone label shown under the name, e.g. 'GMT/BST'.

end.description: Close hour in UTC (0-24). If end <= start the session wraps past midnight.

tone.description: Color tone for the band (maps to a theme-aware token); use one per session.

overlaps.description: High-liquidity overlap windows to highlight on the track, e.g. London+New York 12:00-16:00. Optional; if omitted no overlaps are drawn.

label.description: Short overlap label, e.g. 'London + New York'.

caption.description: One or two sentences delivering the takeaway — name the specific overlap window and why it matters for intraday execution (liquidity, tighter spreads, larger ranges).
